README.md.block:
### Read classic quizzes from the terminal

List a course’s classic quizzes, then inspect one returned quiz ID:

```bash
canvaspilot quizzes 42
canvaspilot quiz 42 9
```

Both commands accept the existing `--base-url`, `--profile` and `--token` options.
Course and quiz IDs must be positive numeric Canvas IDs. `quizzes` uses the existing
paginated reader and compact list fields; `quiz` returns the original detail JSON,
including any supplied timing, attempt-policy, lock and differentiated-date fields.
Null dates and false/zero values keep their original meaning. A failed read exits
nonzero with a JSON error on stderr and no partial success output.

These commands call only the existing [classic-quiz GET endpoints](https://developerdocs.instructure.com/services/canvas/resources/quizzes).
They do not start or complete an attempt, read questions, or change submissions.
New Quizzes and LTI assessments retain the existing separate support boundary.

Read selected courses from the terminal with `canvaspilot announcements 42 77`.
Choose `--detail full` for complete cleaned message text and optionally supply
`--start-date 2026-10-01`. The command preserves the existing course context,
pagination and date-window rules; see [terminal announcement review](docs/announcements-cli.md)
for fields, defaults and error behavior.

src/canvaspilot/cli.py.block:
announcements = sub.add_parser(
        "announcements", help="Read active announcements for selected courses",
    )
    add_common(announcements)
    announcements.add_argument("course_ids", nargs="+", type=_positive_int)
    announcements.add_argument(
        "--start-date", default=None,
        help="Canvas start_date filter (YYYY-MM-DD or ISO 8601); omitted uses Canvas defaults",
    )
    announcements.add_argument(
        "--detail", choices=("compact", "full"), default="compact",
        help="compact limits message text to 400 characters; full keeps the complete stripped text",
    )

quizzes = sub.add_parser("quizzes", help="List classic quizzes for a course")
    add_common(quizzes)
    quizzes.add_argument("course_id", type=_positive_int, help="Positive numeric Canvas course ID")

    quiz = sub.add_parser("quiz", help="Read one classic quiz without starting an attempt")
    add_common(quiz)
    quiz.add_argument("course_id", type=_positive_int, help="Positive numeric Canvas course ID")
    quiz.add_argument("quiz_id", type=_positive_int, help="Positive numeric Canvas quiz ID")

blocks.block:
### Save a readable feedback sheet

```bash
canvaspilot export-feedback 41 902 --out feedback.html
```

Save the selected assignment's self-submission feedback as one HTML file you can
open locally or print. The sheet keeps reported grades beside their attempt
context, including a prominent warning when grading preceded a resubmission.
Rubric criteria retain their returned order and assessments; unmatched entries
stay separate. Comments keep supplied author names, timestamps and literal text,
including media-only entries. Attachment names and media identifiers are listed
when returned; their contents remain in Canvas.

The export uses the same reader and authentication as `feedback`. It distinguishes
zero, unknown values and explicitly empty feedback. Rubric point visibility and
rubric total visibility are applied separately, without changing the separately
reported submission grade. It calculates no grade or rubric total.

Choose a new output path: existing files, directories and symlinks are protected,
including a destination created while the feedback is being read. The completed
file contains its own styling, no scripts or automatic network resources, and
does not refresh. See [the feedback export guide](docs/feedback-export.md) for the
file's contents, exact display rules, local-file behavior and Python usage.

feedback_export = sub.add_parser(
        "export-feedback", help="Save self submission feedback to a new local HTML file",
    )
    add_common(feedback_export)
    feedback_export.add_argument("course_id", type=_positive_int)
    feedback_export.add_argument("assignment_id", type=_positive_int)
    feedback_export.add_argument("--out", required=True, type=Path,
                                 help="New HTML file; existing paths are protected")
